items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: I started playing with his dance band around 57. Mm-hmm. And started playing with his brass band, must have been around 58 to 59.

ctx.x: That's a singer Willie Jackson you're doing? A dancer and a singer, yeah. He was funny. His records are funny. His records are funny. You heard it? Oh yeah, you never heard it? No. I'm a New Orleans Willie Jackson, Old New Orleans Blues Canyon. I don't know. I don't know.
I don't know. It's John of Columbia.
It's in the... I never heard of that record. Yeah. It's in jazz directory. It should be volume five I think.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: I worked with him on the Roof Garden, Maurice Durand and I, and Buddy Johnson... We worked on the Roof Garden two years from 25 to 27.

ctx.x: How was Manuel Perez? Some people talk like he was the greatest of ever, and others say that he wasn't such a hot trumpet player, just a note reader, and that he really couldn't think anything. How did you like him? What did he sound like? He was a legitimate trumpet player.

Much more legitimate. Yeah, yeah. He wasn't a hot trumpet player, not a jazz trumpet player like of today. That's right, strictly music. That's right, a legitimate trumpet player. Did he have a big tone or? Nice tone, kind of nice tone. But it wasn't a fine tone, you know. It was more of a brass band tone, you see. Yeah. Kind of rough, you know. Loud, high notes. Notes didn't come too high, you see. Fine musician. Yeah, that's what I've heard. Yeah, I worked with him on the Roof Garden, Maurice Durand and I, and…
Who was the alto player? Was it before Tad's or after him?

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Harrison Barnes on trombone, Buddy Johnson on trombone, Joe Pye, George Hooker.

ctx.x: And who'd you say was a guitar player, a banjo player? Buddy Manatee. Buddy Manatee and Simon. And Simon. And no piano, of course. No. No violin. No. No.

Now that trombone, I can't place where it was. It might have been yanked. It might have been. I'm not sure. Yanked Johnson. Uh-huh. Trying to see who else was the nice trombone player on at that time. I know he had George Washington later. Oh, yeah. He was out way later. That way. I can't picture who that was. No. No. He never even used Joe. He couldn't play, you know.
Joe played with one joe. No. He couldn't play, you know.
